Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Sudden-onset left-sided headache beginning ~4 h prior to call; no clear external trigger reported (no food, medication, or environmental exposure).
- Symptom timeline and progression: Abrupt onset this morning; pain intensity rated 6/10 (kidney‐stone pain = 10/10). Paracetamol taken ~3 h ago with no relief. Headache worsens with movement, improved by lying still.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: None  
  • Voice change: None  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: None  
  • Nasal/ocular: Blurred vision with zig-zag lines; photophobia (cannot tolerate screens)  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: None  
  • Swelling (lips/tongue/face): None  
  • Ear symptoms: None  
  • Neck pain/swelling: None  
  • Dizziness reported; no limb weakness; gait normal.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: First episode of this type. Two episodes of vomiting at onset; no prior ED visits for similar problem.
- Allergies: Denies known drug allergies.
- Current medications: None routinely. Self-administered paracetamol (dose/route not documented) today.
- Relevant past medical history: Prior kidney stones. No chronic conditions reported.
- Family history: Mother – migraine and hypothyroidism.
- Social context: Tele-consultation; patient at home, alone (no supervision mentioned).

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None noted/reported via video link.
- Airway/breathing: Speaking in full sentences; no noisy breathing.
- Mental status: Alert, appropriately interactive; reports dizziness but denies confusion, weakness, gait change.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (tele-visit).
- Accompaniment: Not documented.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Probable migraine with aura.
  Evidence: Unilateral headache, visual zig-zag lines, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, family history, no focal neurological deficits.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  1. Migraine with aura – high likelihood; fits classic features.
  2. Subarachnoid haemorrhage – medium likelihood; sudden first headache with nausea/vomiting, but pain moderate (6/10), no “worst ever,” no neuro deficit.
  3. Carotid/vertebral artery dissection – low–medium; unilateral pain and visual disturbance, but no neck pain/trauma or focal deficits.
- No conflict between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Pharmacologic trial: Advise ibuprofen (OTC dosing per pharmacist guidance) plus OTC anti-emetic and oral sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola) as initial migraine regimen.
- Follow-up: Same-day in-person appointment for full neurological examination; patient to cancel if symptoms fully resolve before visit.
- Escalation/red flags: Call emergency services or attend ED immediately for sudden worsening headache, “worst ever” pain, new visual loss, weakness, speech difficulty, confusion, persistent vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down.
- General advice: Rest in dark quiet room, maintain hydration, avoid excessive screen use. Keep symptom diary if recurrent.
- Future considerations (if migraines confirmed): Discuss specific migraine abortive/preventive therapies at follow-up; consider referral to neurology.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Objective vitals (BP, HR, temp), detailed neurological and fundoscopic exam, medication doses/routes, pregnancy test (though low suspicion), documentation of photophobia/phonophobia formally, comprehensive medication/allergy list confirmation.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor connectivity interruptions but clinical data intelligible.
